findings.title: TypeError when destinationCalendar is empty array on Meet bookings
findings.body: The new fallback that decides whether to switch the meeting location to Cal Video no longer uses optional chaining. Line 119 destructures `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` into `mainHostDestinationCalendar`, and line 120 reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` directly. When `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, `undefined`, or an empty array (a normal state for many bookings), the destructured variable is `undefined` and accessing `.integration` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')`. The previous code (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`) safely evaluated to `true` in that case. Any booking whose `location` is Google Meet and that has no destinationCalendar configured will now crash with 500 instead of silently falling back to Cal Video.

findings.title: Collective events silently drop all host destination calendars when organizer has none
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized as `null` when neither the event-type nor the organizer user has one (see the `evt = { ... destinationCalendar: ... ? [...] : null }` block around line 1067). The subsequent `if (isTeamEventType && eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE") { evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars); }` uses optional chaining, so the push becomes a no-op when the value is `null`. As a result, collective bookings that have no event-type-level or organizer-level destination calendar end up with an empty/null `destinationCalendar`, and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` falls through to the `cred.type === "calendar"` branch which never matches real credentials (`google_calendar`, etc.). The expected per-host calendar invitations for that scenario are silently lost.

findings.title: Only the first destination calendar of a collective booking is persisted on the Booking row
findings.body: When writing the new booking row, the change connects only `evt.destinationCalendar[0].id` to the booking's `destinationCalendar` relation: `destinationCalendar: evt.destinationCalendar && evt.destinationCalendar.length > 0 ? { connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id } } : undefined`. For collective events the array now contains the organizer plus every host's destination calendar (built up by the `teamDestinationCalendars` push on line 1078), but the Booking schema only stores the first entry. Any later code path that consults `booking.destinationCalendar` directly (instead of `booking.references`, e.g. confirm.handler.ts, editLocation.handler.ts, handleCancelBooking.ts at line ~251, paypal-webhook.ts line 152, deleteCredential.handler.ts line 290) will only see the organizer's calendar and lose information about the other hosts. This contradicts the PR description that the booking now supports multiple destinations per host.

findings.title: Google Calendar updateEvent passes undefined calendarId when no externalCalendarId is supplied
findings.body: Inside `updateEvent` the new selection is `selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. The `find` callback compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId`, but the parent ternary only enters this branch when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (typically `undefined`), so `find` matches nothing and returns `undefined`. The previous code simply used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` and worked for any single-destination booking. As a result, callers like `CalendarManager.updateEvent` (which always omits `externalCalendarId`) now send `calendarId: undefined` to the Google Calendar API, causing the update to 404 even though the destination calendar is present on the event.

findings.title: Google Calendar deleteEvent always deletes from "primary" when externalCalendarId is omitted
findings.body: `deleteEvent` uses the same `find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` lookup as `updateEvent`. With `externalCalendarId` undefined (the only form `CalendarManager.deleteEvent` ever calls it with), the lookup never matches and the fallback `calendarId: calendarId ? calendarId : defaultCalendarId` resolves to `"primary"`. Previously it just used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. Bookings whose host's destination calendar is not the user's Google primary calendar will now be deleted from the wrong calendar; for events that don't exist on primary, the 404/410 path silently resolves and the real calendar event is orphaned.

findings.title: requestReschedule drops user fallback for destinationCalendar (inconsistent with other handlers)
findings.body: The new assignment is `destinationCalendar: bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar ? [bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar] : []`. Every other handler in the PR (confirm.handler.ts:175, editLocation.handler.ts:85, handleCancelBooking.ts:251, deleteCredential.handler.ts:290, handleNewBooking.ts:1063) falls back to `user.destinationCalendar` when the booking has none. Here that fallback was removed (it was a typo'd duplicate in the old code), so reschedule webhooks and the reschedule email are now sent with `destinationCalendar: []` even when the booking's owner has a destination calendar configured. This is inconsistent and may mislead recipients about which calendar will be updated.

findings.title: No test covers the core multi-host destinationCalendar fix
findings.body: The PR author checked the box "I haven't added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works." The only test change in the whole PR is updating the expected `destinationCalendar` value from `null` to `[]` in `apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts`. There is no integration or unit test exercising the new collective-event path: building the `evt.destinationCalendar` array with organizer + team host destinations, persisting it through `handleNewBooking`, or verifying that `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` fans out to all host calendars. Given the size of the refactor (signatures changed, persistence narrowed, multiple CalendarService adapters updated), this is a significant test gap and the regressions called out above (e.g. TypeError on Meet bookings, dropped team destinations, broken Google update/delete) are likely to pass through CI because nothing in the suite exercises the scenario.
